title: Driving, Fast or Slow? Neuro-Symbolic Guidance for Motion Prediction in Multi-Modal Ground Mobility
abstract: arXiv:2606.15251v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Accurate and interpretable motion prediction for heterogeneous traffic spaces, including pedestrians, bicycles, cars, and trucks, is essential for safe autonomous navigation. Nevertheless, state-of-the-art approaches remain predominantly black-box, lacking explicit encoding of the regulatory and behavioral constraints of real-world mobility. We propose Trajectory Compliance-Shaping (TraCS), a neuro-symbolic framework that augments existing black-box motion prediction backbones with interpretable and probabilistic first-order logic. To do so, TraCS employs an agentic code-generation pipeline to bridge the gap between natural-language descriptions of traffic regulations and probabilistic motion prediction. Furthermore, TraCS employs a reactive data-streaming inference engine that maintains and efficiently updates compliance landscapes as scenes evolve. translated_title: 驾驶，该快还是该慢？面向多模态地面移动的运动预测神经符号引导方法
translated_abstract: 对包括行人、自行车、汽车和卡车在内的异构交通空间进行准确且可解释的运动预测，对于安全的自主导航至关重要。然而，最先进的方法仍然主要是黑盒式的，缺乏对现实世界移动中法规和行为约束的显式编码。我们提出了轨迹合规性塑造，这是一个神经符号框架，它利用可解释的概率一阶逻辑来增强现有的黑盒运动预测主干模型。为此，TraCS 采用代理式代码生成流程，以弥合交通法规的自然语言描述与概率运动预测之间的鸿沟。此外，TraCS 还采用了一个响应式数据流推理引擎，能够随着场景的演变维护并高效更新合规性图景。为防止 TraCS 过度自信地引导主干模型的预测……
tldr: 提出了TraCS神经符号框架，通过代理式代码生成将自然语言交通法规转化为可解释的概率一阶逻辑约束，并利用响应式数据流推理引擎实时更新合规性图景，从而增强黑盒运动预测模型在异构交通环境中的可解释性与安全性。
en_tdlr: TraCS is a neuro-symbolic framework that augments black-box motion prediction backbones with interpretable probabilistic first-order logic, using an agentic code-generation pipeline to translate natural-language traffic regulations into constraints and a reactive data-streaming inference engine to update compliance landscapes in real time.
